instructions: StationGod reads and changes a running Stationeers world. Each tool is a verb; most take what (the kind of thing) and share option names: find (lists), inspect (one thing in detail), survey (an area or network), read (live values), write (set values), plan (work out, change nothing), check (rules), build, swap (existing pieces), remove, move, trade, show (draw for the player), undo, server. help {verb, what} gives one in full. Targets: id (one, a list, or a ref "r3" from an earlier reply), near + radius, box, room, network. 'this', 'that' or 'here' is the thing the crosshair is on: inspect {what: "looking_at"}. Typed ids act at once; build, swap, remove, trade, undo and cheats report until confirm: true, and so does any write given a ref, network or spread; ask the user before a cheat. Shaping on every verb: fields, omit, list_limits, output_file, repeat (a ref: that call again), whole: true (lifts the 12 KB cut). Multiplayer: as_player (a name or id) on any verb says who "the player" is (near "player", looking_at, materials "player", show); show without it draws for every player. For waits, polls and timed or repeated work, run_script; for many targets, give id a list. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. If the user says stop or hold: server {what: 'stop'} (load the server tool if it isn't).

tools.name: find
tools.description: List things in the world or an area, filtered, nearest first. Read only.

what.description: thing: any object: structures, devices, items, players; item: stackable items and kits anywhere; group_by sums; device: devices with logic; container: holders with items; frame: outer frames; pad: landing pads; water: water and steam sources; ore: deep miner ore spots; food: food and drink; plant: plants: stage, health, harvest; room: closed rooms: pressure, gases; gateway: device scopes (gateways); damaged: damaged and broken things; void: underground pockets to fill; script: saved scripts; ghost: planned structures (ghosts); lattice: ask Lattice

prefab.description: Whole name, hash, or parts with * ('*Tank*Insulated*'); or a list.

text.description: find script: text a saved script's name or description holds.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Describe one thing, or a few by id, in detail. Read only.

what.description: device: a device's logic types; prefab: a prefab before it is built; slots: a device's slots; contents: a holder's contents, nested; health: damage of things or a network; connections: a piece's ends and joins; atmosphere: the gas one thing holds; reagents: a machine's reagents; genes: plant genes; chip: a chip's status, source, selectors; screen: a screen's surfaces and elements; rocket: rockets now; vault: Ingot Vault stock; looking_at: what the crosshair is on; player: the player's hunger and thirst; planet: the planet's atmosphere; weather: storms and season; job: a job or script run, by id; controllers: what writes or overrides a device; script: one saved script

name.description: inspect script: the saved script's name; inspect contents: a display name to match.

tools.name: survey
tools.description: Map an area or a network as a whole: the grid's cells, a wall face, a network's members, feed paths. Read only.

what.description: area: the 2 m cells of a box or room: what occupies each, the pieces, devices, ports and networks; wall: a text elevation of one 2 m face plane, 0.5 m per character; free_rects finds where a rectangle fits; network: a cable, pipe or chute network's members (or the pieces in a box), with filters or a summary; feeds: how a network feeds its devices from a root device: pieces and rooms each feed passes, daisy chains, unreached devices

box.description: area: Two corners; at most 20000 2 m cells. network: Box form: the pieces in it (alone: open ends in it).

network.description: area: Only pieces on these networks. network, feeds: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.

prefab.description: area: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them. network: Only members whose prefab holds this part.

cell_detail.description: occupancy: cells {at, empty, frame_id, faces, small}; full: cells {at, room_id, frame, walls, small, support} in place of those. Default occupancy.

half_width.description: Half-width of the map in metres. Default 4.

free_rects.description: {w, h, one_section, require_wall, limit}: where a w x h rectangle fits.

near.description: Centre: [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position); with radius.

id.description: The root device (an APC output, a generator). Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read live values: logic, memory, a snapshot, samples over time, the clock, flight logs. Read only.

what.description: logic: logic values; slots, atmosphere, reagents in one frame; snapshot: every logic value of matching devices; memory: a device's memory; sample: values over up to 30 s; clock: game time; flight_log: flight recorder rows

tools.name: write
tools.description: Set values and states. Typed ids act at once; a ref or network reports until confirm: true. memory, battery, genes and health are cheats: ask the user.

what.description: logic: logic values on devices; memory: device memory; chip: chip source, pins, run state; screen: press a screen control; label: rename things; paint: paint things or a network; flight_log: start, stop, clear a recorder; uplink: point an uplink; battery: set charge; genes: edit plant genes; health: heal a player; script: save a script; lattice: Lattice commands

allow.description: lint: pass a network lint problem.

code.description: write chip: the IC10 source; write script: the Python source, which must define main(...).

name.description: write script: the script's name (letters, digits, underscores).

description.description: write script: one line saying what the script does.

scope.description: write script: shared (any world, no hard-coded ids), or world (bound to this world).

tools.name: plan
tools.description: Work out how, changing nothing: routes, removal prices, free spots, rocket flights, mining yields, aim angles. Read only.

what.description: route: cable, pipe or chute route; removal: removal price; spot: free spots for a prefab; flight: rocket flight and landing check; mining: rocket mining yield; aim: solar panel or dish angles

tools.name: check
tools.description: Check against rules and risks: the layout lint of a room or box, the lint rule set, whether things are replaceable, the player's ignition risk. Read only.

what.description: layout: lint a room or a box against the layout rules: replaceability, doors, ports, floating runs, overlaps and more; rules: the lint rule set: list, validate a file, fields, functions, run examples, explain a finding; replaceable: could a player place each thing again exactly where it stands, every neighbour present; ignition: whether carried items, or a tank or network by id, would catch fire in the air around them

box.description: Two corners; at most 4000 2 m cells.

id.description: layout: Narrows: only findings on these things (up to 256); room or box is still needed. rules: explain: a thing, network or room id. replaceable: Things to check (1 to 1024); a list answers one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error. ignition: A tank, canister or pipe network: its contents' autoignition margin, a list one row each; left out, the player's carried items.

tools.name: build
tools.description: Build new things as a player would, paying materials. Reports first; confirm: true builds and answers when the job is done. terrain and item are cheats: ask the user.

what.description: structure: any structure a kit builds, at a point; cable: a run or pieces; pipe: a run or pieces; chute: a run or pieces; blueprint: paste a blueprint; terrain: fill or level terrain; item: make items by prefab (a cheat); finish: a placed structure to a later state

from_plan.description: A plan route or spot ref ('r9'): build its build_arguments; options given win, what may be left out.

grade.description: cable: default heavy; pipe: required; chute: chute.

tools.name: swap
tools.description: Swap things already built, in place: walls or frames, upgrade or tidy cable, pipe and chute networks. Reports first; confirm: true does it.

what.description: wall: replace walls and windows with another wall or window prefab without opening a face; frame: replace frames with another frame prefab, or finish unfinished frames, without opening a cell; cable: upgrade cable in place (into heavy or super_heavy) or tidy a network (tidy: remove dead ends, loops...); pipe: upgrade pipe in place (into insulated, or repair burst pieces) or tidy a network, keeping its contents; chute: remove chute pieces no item can pass to a consumer; junctions left with one way become straights

id.description: frame, pipe, chute: An id, a list, a ref ('r3'), or "looking_at". cable: Pieces (up to 4096). Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error.

into.description: wall: The new wall prefab. frame: The new frame prefab; default each frame's own (finishes it). cable: Upgrade to this grade; heavy when tidy is left out. pipe: insulated, or repair: burst pieces become new; insulated when tidy is left out.

prefab.description: wall: Only pieces of these prefabs; the others are kept. frame: Only pieces of these prefabs.

materials.description: Holder(s) that pay, in order; ids or "player".

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

network.description: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.

tidy.description: cable: Tidy operations, alone or together; true is [simplify_junctions]. pipe: Tidy operations; true is [simplify_junctions].

box.description: Every chute piece in the box (at most a 32 m cube).

riding.description: A piece holding an item: skip it, or refuse the run. Default skip.

tools.name: remove
tools.description: Take things away as a player would, with refunds and guards. Reports first; confirm: true removes and answers when the job is done. terrain is a cheat: ask the user.

what.description: structure: built structures by id or every one in a box (up to 256, one job), taken apart; every build state is refunded down to the kit; cable: cable pieces as wire cutters remove them: by id, or the piece in each cell of waypoints or cells; pipe: pipe pieces as a player remove them: by id, or the piece in each cell of waypoints or cells, never emptying or splitting a network that holds gas; chute: chute pieces as a player remove them: by id, or the piece in each cell of waypoints or cells; terrain: dig out a box of terrain; script: delete a saved script

id.description: structure: The structures. cable, pipe, chute: Pieces. Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error.

materials.description: structure: The one holder for source and storage refunds: an id or "player". Default the player. cable, pipe, chute: Holder(s) that pay, in order; ids or "player".

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

waypoints.description: The piece in every cell along these lines.

name.description: remove script: the saved script's name.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Move items, gas and players. Items by typed ids move at once; a ref or a filter reports until confirm: true. gas and player are cheats: ask the user.

what.description: item: items and kits into a slot, the player, or a vault or silo; gas: gas between atmospheres, or delete it; player: a player to a point, thing or player

to.description: item: the holder that gets them (a vault or silo makes a store move). gas: a thing or room.

source.description: item: a vault or silo. gas: a thing, room, planet, or create.

tools.name: trade
tools.description: Trade with traders: contacts in the sky, what each buys and sells, and buying or selling with the landed trader. buy and sell report until confirm: true.

what.description: contacts: every trader contact in the sky and every satellite dish with where it points; inventory: what each contact buys and sells: prices, stock, conditions, and what you hold that meets them; buy: buy from the landed trader as the trade window's Buy does; sell: sell to the landed trader as the trade window's Sell does

id.description: inventory: One contact; left out, every contact. buy, sell: The trader contact. Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error.

card.description: inventory: The card whose holder's goods count; default the player's. buy: The credit card; default the one the player carries. sell: The credit card paid into; default the one the player carries.

items.description: buy: Up to 32 lines {name or prefab, quantity}, in order. sell: Up to 32 lines {name or prefab, quantity}.

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Draw on the player's screen only, for a while: a build preview (wire boxes or ghosts of the structures), or highlights through walls. Nothing in the world changes.

what.description: preview: a planned structure layout or cable, pipe or chute run (build's dry run) as wire boxes or see-through ghosts, plus cells and boxes; highlight: show the player where things, a network or far points are, tinted and labelled; ghost: persistent ghosts on the board; lattice: Lattice's local view

prefab.description: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them.

run.description: A cable, pipe or chute run to plan and draw: build's options with what.

from_plan.description: A plan route or spot ref ('r9'): preview its build_arguments.

style.description: boxes (default), ghost (the structures' own meshes, see-through) or both.

targets.description: Up to 64, each one of {id (one or a list), network, at} with color, label, pulse.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo a finished build or removal job, a bulk write (write-N), a script run (script-14: the whole run, newest first), or the newest blueprint paste. Reports first; confirm: true undoes.

id.description: The job, the bulk write (write-N), the script run (script-14), or "paste" on its own; a list is undone newest first, in one report.

materials.description: The one holder every call pays from and refunds to. Default the job's own recorded source, else the player; never filled in by the verb layer.

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

tools.name: server
tools.description: StationGod and the game server: mod version, health and costs, profiling, the in-game console. command is a cheat.

what.description: info: the running mod: version, per-method calls and times, game members, its cost to the game, the cheat switch; profiling: profile StationGod's main-thread cost: on, off, reset, report; console: the latest in-game console lines, oldest first; command: run any console command and answer what it printed: spawn, delete, teleport, storms, settings; stop: stop a script run or drop a waiting job; no id: every run

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

id.description: The run or job to stop: 'script-14'. Left out: every live run.

tools.name: help
tools.description: StationGod's help, from the MCP server: help {} lists verbs and topics; {verb} a verb's whats and options; {verb, what} one what in full; {topic} a shared topic.

lang.description: python: the stub for sg calls in a script; leave it out for a direct call.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description:
Run Python 3.10 against the game: one call made of verb calls. sg.<verb>('what', **options) is the direct call with the same options and reply dicts: one id answers the one-id shape, an id list {results: [...]}.
A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. Seen targets: ids this session's replies showed you (report rows and a finished run's printed or returned value count), ids the run's own reads answered, int or str constants in the code, selectors in the code (a network, a spread, sg.ref('r7')), what the run builds, and "player". Two routes:
- run_script {code}: a report run. Nothing changes; every target is listed [id or cell, name, current -> new] (the footer shows 10 per write and counts the rest; inspect {what: 'job', id, whole: true} shows all). To act, send the same code with confirm: true: its rows are now seen.
- run_script {code, confirm: true}: acts as it goes on seen targets. An unseen target stops the run with sg.Stopped (a BaseException); the reply lists that call's targets (now seen), what acted, and the fix.
confirm inside the code is refused.
Saved scripts: write script saves Python under a name, find script lists them, inspect script shows one in full, and run_script {name, args} runs its main(**args). The arguments are checked against main's signature before the run: a missing required argument or an unknown name is a refusal, and a value's type too where the annotation maps one; a list's items and anything else are left to the run. A shared script may hard-code no ids; a world script runs only in the world it was saved in. The journal records the version it ran.
Poll, and put things back:
  sg.write('logic', id=ff, logic='Open', value=1)
  try:
      while sg.read('logic', reads=[{'id': probe, 'atmosphere': True}])['results'][0]['atmosphere']['pressure_kpa'] < 15:
          sg.wait(5)        # poll a sensor with read; a room or find query walks the world
  finally:
      sg.write('logic', id=ff, logic='Open', value=0)   # best effort at session end
  # sure, even at session end: with sg.hold(ff, 'Open', 1, after=0): ...
A confirmed run answers within 30 s, then script-N running (follow with inspect {what: 'job', id}); a report or read-only run waits up to 600 s. sg.help('scripts') has the full API; errors raise sg.Error(code, message, fix, maybe_ran).
Footer: writes by outcome, WARNINGS (alike ones once, with a count), CLEANUP, undo script-N, cost.

code.description: Python 3.10 source, run as a function body.

name.description: A saved script to run with args; exactly one of code or name.

args.description: The saved script's main(...) arguments by name; checked before the run.

confirm.description: true: writes act, on seen targets. Left out: a report run; nothing changes.

max_wait.description: How long this reply waits; at most 30 s for a confirmed run.
